text: Should I patent or trademark my Ayurvedic product? Patent protects the INVENTION (novel formulation, process, device) for 20 years but requires disclosure and proving novelty. Trademark protects the BRAND NAME (like Chyawanprash, Dabur, Patanjali) indefinitely as long as renewed and used. For most Ayurvedic products based on classical formulations, trademark protection for brand name is more practical since the formulation itself may not be patentable. You can have BOTH - patent on novel formulation AND trademark on brand name.

Can I keep my Ayurvedic formulation as trade secret instead of patent? Yes, trade secrets protect confidential business information without disclosure. Famous examples include Coca-Cola formula. For Ayurvedic formulations, trade secret is viable if: (1) the formulation cannot be reverse-engineered easily, (2) you can maintain confidentiality with employees/manufacturers, (3) you don't need to disclose for regulatory approval. However, once disclosed (e.g., for ASU license), trade secret protection is lost. Trade secrets have no expiry but no legal protection if independently discovered by others.

How does ASU drug license relate to patents? Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani (ASU) drugs are regulated under Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940 and Rules 1945. Getting drug license requires disclosure of formulation to licensing authority. This disclosure does NOT affect patent rights if patent application was filed BEFORE license application. Recommended sequence: (1) File patent application first, (2) Then apply for ASU license. Once patent is granted, competitors cannot manufacture your patented formulation even if they have drug license for similar products.

Are clinical trials needed for Ayurvedic patents and products? For PATENT: Clinical trials are not mandatory but providing clinical evidence of efficacy greatly strengthens the patent, especially to overcome Section 3(d) objections for enhanced efficacy. For ASU LICENSE: Classical formulations (in Schedule E1 books) don't require clinical trials for licensing. Proprietary formulations need safety and efficacy data but full clinical trials may be waived depending on ingredients. For CLAIMS: Any specific therapeutic claim on product requires supporting clinical evidence as per Drugs and Magic Remedies Act.

Can Ayurvedic products get Geographical Indication (GI) tag? Yes, if the product is unique to a specific region and derives qualities from that geography. Examples relevant to AYUSH: Darjeeling Tea (GI), Kashmir Saffron (GI), Marayoor Jaggery (GI). For traditional medicine, a formulation associated with a specific region's traditional practice could potentially get GI protection. GI is a collective right - registered by a group/association, not individuals.

How do I file international patents for my AYUSH invention? Options: (1) Paris Convention route: File in India first, then file in each desired country within 12 months claiming priority; (2) PCT route: File international application (via Indian Patent Office), enters national phase in desired countries within 30/31 months. PCT is cost-effective if filing in 3+ countries. Note: Section 3(p) plant exclusion is specific to India - some countries may allow plant patents. US allows plant patents; EU has plant variety rights. Strategy: Design claims to focus on patentable aspects (process, formulation, use) that work across jurisdictions.

Typical costs for patent filing in India for AYUSH startups/individuals: (1) Government fees (e-filing, startup): ~Rs 4,000 filing + Rs 10,000 RFE = ~Rs 14,000 base; (2) Patent attorney/agent fees: Rs 15,000-50,000 depending on complexity; (3) Total first-year cost: Rs 20,000-65,000. Additional costs: response to examination reports (Rs 5,000-20,000 each), grant fee, annual renewal fees. For startup with limited budget: Consider filing provisional application first (lower initial cost, 12 months to file complete specification), use startup fee category, consider DIY filing for simple inventions using IPO's online system.

Should I file provisional or complete patent application? Provisional application: Lower fee, establishes priority date, gives 12 months to file complete specification with experimental data. Useful when: invention is at early stage, need to secure date before publication/disclosure, still conducting experiments. Complete application: Full protection from day one, can proceed directly to examination. Required: complete specification with claims, abstract, drawings if any. For AYUSH: If your formulation is ready and tested, file complete directly. If still optimizing or conducting trials, file provisional first.

How do I conduct prior art search before filing AYUSH patent? Free resources: (1) Indian Patent Office website - InPASS search; (2) Google Patents; (3) USPTO PatFT/AppFT; (4) Espacenet (EPO); (5) WIPO Patentscope. For traditional knowledge: (6) Search classical Ayurvedic texts; (7) Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India; (8) Published research papers on PubMed, Google Scholar. Red flags: If your formulation is mentioned in any classical text or published paper, it may not be novel. Focus your patent on the MODIFICATION or IMPROVEMENT over known formulations.

Do I need a patent agent for filing? Legally, you CAN file patent application yourself (pro se filing) through IPO's online system. However, patent agent is recommended because: (1) Proper claim drafting is critical - poorly drafted claims may not provide protection; (2) Prosecution (responding to objections) requires legal and technical expertise; (3) For AYUSH patents, handling Section 3(d), 3(e), 3(p) objections needs experience. Patent agents must pass Patent Agent Exam conducted by IPO. Verify registration at IPO website. Attorney fees are investment in protecting your innovation.
